facts.text: [L4] **The scalar field** ([[def-field]], [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]): in $\mathbb C$ only nonzero elements have multiplicative inverses; the expression $0^{-1}$ and the quotient $0/0$ are not defined, and the formula for $\nu$ is a scalar multiplication by the inverse of the norm.

proof_used_steps.claim: [Normalization is undefined] The normalization formula $\nu(\psi)=\|\psi\|^{-1}\psi$ uses the inverse of the scalar $\|\psi\|$; at $\psi=0$ this inverse would be $0^{-1}$, which does not exist in $\mathbb C$ by [L4], and the displayed "convention" $0/\|0\|=0$ is therefore not an instance of the definition but a separate stipulation. Even granting the stipulation its value, $\|0\|=0\ne1$ by [L2], so it does not produce a unit representative; the stipulation is self-defeating as a normalization rule.
